newsitem.title: USA: Rawlings putting its name on sports drink line.
newsitem.headline: Rawlings putting its name on sports drink line.

text.p: Rawlings Sporting Goods Co., probably best known for baseballs and other sporting equipment, is putting its name on a new line of sport drinks, the company said Wednesday.

The new beverage, Rawlings Sport a New Age, will be introduced in May. It will be followed starting in June by Rawlings for Kids and Rawlings Natural Spring Water, according to David Brawley, director of licensing for St. Louis-based Rawlings.
The beverages will be produced and marketed by Beverage Source International Inc. (BSI), a unit of Sharon Real Estate Consultants Corp.
"They approached us. We were thrilled when they did," Brawley said.
Rawlings Sport, which is fortified with vitamins and minerals to replenish electrolytes and nutrients, will carry the motto, "The Mark of a Pro."
BSI and Rawlings plan a worldwide co-marketing campaign lead by BSI, which will include endorsements from Rawlings' roster of professional athletes and cross-marketing of products.
Brawley said he expects the beverage line will help promote the Rawlings name to consumers. In addition, Brawley said, "it really has a potential to be a very serious money maker."
Rawlings' earnings from the beverage line will come from licensing its brand.
The sports drink business, however, is dominated by Quaker Oats Co.'s Gatorade, with more than $1.0 billion in sales in the United States in 1996 and an 81 percent market share.
Other players in the sports beverage business include Coca-Cola Co.'s PowerAde and PepsiCo's All Sport.
Despite such heavy-hitting competition, Rawlings hopes to capture a niche market position, such as its sports drink for children, which will feature an eight-ounce sports bottle, the company said.
